title: Inquest says Mounties should review training
article: A coroner's inquest into the shooting death of a man by police near Kamloops, B.C.. has recommended Mounties review a training video on shooting at vehicles.
The inquest looked into the death of 45-year-old Stephen Mace Hanaghan in June 2005.
He was shot after he rammed his truck into a police car following a chase. The inquest jury says Hanaghan died from internal bleeding caused by a single gunshot wound to his left flank.
It ruled his death a homicide, a neutral term meaning it was caused by another person.

The jury recommend Mounties review a training video on dangerous tactic-shooting at vehicles on a regular basis, and that they carry a basic first aid kit that includes an air mask and mouthpiece for CPR. (CHNL)
